item.title: Is the Iran War Entering a Dangerous New Phase?
item.description: Escalating U.S.-Iran strikes are widening the conflict beyond the Strait of Hormuz, threatening Gulf infrastructure, regional stability, and global energy security. Yet behind the fighting, mediators are searching for an off-ramp before the crisis spirals further.

item.title: Ending Forced Labor: Comparing EU and U.S. Approaches
item.description: The European Union’s new Forced Labor Regulation joins U.S. import bans in targeting goods made with forced labor. The effectiveness of both approaches will depend on credible enforcement, strong due diligence and reporting mechanisms, and meaningful worker engagement.

item.title: America’s Unproven Productivity Boom, and the Cost of Misreading the Data
item.description: The recent boom in U.S. labor productivity may not be early dividends of new AI technologies, but a routine labor market adjustment. Until the data starts to provide a clearer story, policymakers would be wise to consider the jury out to avoid serious policy missteps.

item.title: U.S.-India Insight: The U.S.-India Trade Deal: From Dam to Spark
item.description: The trade deal isn't just a trade deal — it's the key that unlocks the entire US-India relationship.

item.title: Protecting Human Rights at the World Cup: Progress on Paper, Gaps on the Ground
item.description: As the 2026 World Cup draws to a close, this article examines FIFA’s evolving commitments to human rights, its record at recent tournaments, and factors that will determine whether protections for workers, fans, and players improve, stall, or decline at future tournaments.

item.title: Playbook or Rental? U.S. Counter-Drone Defense and the 2026 World Cup
item.description: For the 2026 World Cup, the United States built its first nationwide drone defense in months. Whether the country keeps a counter-drone playbook it can carry forward, or returns a six-week rental once the stadiums empty, is the choice it faces the morning after the final.

item.title: The Trade Transparency Challenge
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch explores how growing demands for trade transparency are reshaping customs, supply chains, and compliance, with implications for businesses, consumers, and global commerce.

item.title: The NATO Ankara Summit: Delivery over Drama
item.description: The NATO Ankara Summit may have lacked dramatic headlines, but it delivered where it mattered most—advancing European defense capabilities, reinforcing support for Ukraine, and demonstrating that Alliance adaptation continues amid strategic uncertainty.
